title: PAYMENT SYSTEM (STRIPE)
subtitle: Throughput is moderate. The hard part is staying correct when a call to the bank has an unknown outcome.
footer: DDIA: Ch 8 unknown outcomes · Ch 12 end-to-end idempotency, integrity · Ch 11 outbox   ·   Similar: Online judge · Job scheduler

items: Record the payment as pending before calling the processor, and pass your ID as the idempotency key.
On a timeout, query by that key or retry it; never create a second charge.
Publish status changes through an outbox, keep an append-only double-entry ledger, and reconcile daily.
Merchants create payment intents; customers pay by card
Merchants receive status via webhooks
Refunds
Never double-charge (exactly-once effect)
Durable and auditable; strongly consistent ledger
~10k TPS
PCI: raw card data isolated
10k TPS is moderate for a well-indexed Postgres cluster.
The hard part is correctness under unknown outcomes, not throughput.

Naive: call the processor, then write the DB. A crash in between charges the card with no record of it.

items: Write the intent as PENDING first, call the processor with our intent ID as the idempotency key, then record the result.
Merchants send an Idempotency-Key on every mutating call (stored with a unique index).
Status changes write an outbox row in the same transaction; a relay publishes and webhooks are delivered with retries and signatures.
Processor times out?
Unknown outcome (DDIA Ch 8): keep PENDING, retry with the same idempotency key or query status by reference.
Webhook delivery?
Outbox in the same transaction; exponential backoff; merchants dedupe by event_id.
Why double-entry?
Every movement is a debit + credit summing to zero, so balances are derivable and auditable; never UPDATE amounts.
Distributed transaction with the bank?
Impossible. Design a state machine with compensation (refund) and reconciliation.
Using 2PC or assuming the processor call succeeds or fails cleanly.
Adding parts before a number shows they are needed.
Ignoring retries, timeouts and crashes.
